name: Artichoke
description: Artichoke (Cynara cardunculus var. scolymus) is a nutrient-dense botanical concentrate, highly valued for its unique phytochemical profile—specifically cynarin and silymarin. Its complex matrix of inulin-type fructans and polyphenolic antioxidants is engineered to modulate hepatic detoxification, stimulate bile kinetics, and optimize the colonic microbiota ecosystem.
macroIntro: A clean, low-calorie carbohydrate framework characterized by a significant prebiotic fiber yield and a near-zero lipid footprint.
microIntro: A highly bioavailable micronutrient matrix featuring essential B-vitamins and mineral cofactors that reinforce systemic vascular stability and regenerative pathways.

healthBenefits: Hepatic Detoxification: Cynarin and Silymarin stimulate hepatocyte regeneration and bolster glutathione-dependent detoxification pathways.
Bile Kinetics: Bitter compounds enhance endogenous bile secretion, optimizing lipid emulsification and cholesterol metabolic clearance.
Prebiotic Colonization: Inulin-type fructans bypass early digestion to selectively proliferate beneficial Bifidobacteria in the distal colon.
Endothelial Protection: Potent polyphenolic fractions neutralize lipid peroxidation, safeguarding vascular flexibility.
precautionsIntro: Nutritional calibration is required for gastrointestinal and metabolic health:
precautions: FODMAP Sensitivity: High inulin content may trigger severe bloating or gas in individuals with IBS or SIBO.
Bile Duct Pathology: Accelerated bile production can trigger biliary colic in patients with significant gallstones or bile duct obstructions.
Industrial Preservation: Canned or marinated artichokes often contain excessive sodium and additives; rinse thoroughly or prioritize fresh/steamed forms.
